title: Tech & architecture slides for the Oriola deck
subtitle: Two slides for deck-writer to insert after the answer-first slide
footer: Recordly | Oriola Oyj | Data warehouse migration to Azure

slides.title: One metadata-driven pipeline pattern replaces hand-crafted wholesale scripts
bullets: Adding a wholesale or warehouse interface = **one config row + tests**, not a new script. The same template runs in every warehouse environment.
Built only in Oriola's Azure tenant and Git; no new per-user licences, only Azure consumption (Data Factory, ADLS, Databricks DBUs).

diagram.band: CI/CD from shared templates · alerts with runbooks so incidents get fixed once, not fire-fought every week

slides.note: Decision point in the pilot: Data Factory vs Databricks ingestion per interface type, picked on measured throughput, not preference.

slides.title: A 6-week pilot on real supply chain tables sets the velocity before any multi-year commitment
table: Tables migrated and reconciled per week (pilot scope: ~30 tables, 2 warehouse interfaces)
Forecast for full estate fits plan ±15%
Row and value reconciliation against the legacy DW for stock, order and invoice measures
Share of interfaces onboarded with config only, no custom code
Failed loads per week, time to recover
bullets: **Technical unknowns we price in:** SAP extraction throughput and authorisations; undocumented logic in the legacy DW; length of the parallel run; GDP traceability of batch/lot data.
Each later wave is sized from the pilot's measured velocity, so the price of the rest is evidence, not a guess.
